## Overview

Just Speak to It now offers NVIDIA Parakeet v3 as a recommended local transcription model. It provides offline, multilingual transcription with automatic language detection, punctuation, and capitalisation, while also improving the reliability and maintainability of the transcription code.

## Highlights

- **New Parakeet v3 local model**
  - Add NVIDIA Parakeet v3 (TDT 0.6B) to the local model catalogue.
  - Supports 25 European languages with automatic language detection.
  - Produces punctuation and capitalisation alongside the transcription.
  - Runs locally through the sherpa-onnx runtime, so audio can be transcribed offline.
  - Provides streaming partial results during recording and a final whole-session transcription when input ends.

- **Clearer local-model setup information**
  - Parakeet v3 is presented as the recommended sherpa-onnx local source.
  - Settings show its supported languages, RAM guidance, and CC-BY-4.0 licence information when it is selected.
  - The model download uses a pinned version and verifies its SHA-256 checksum, helping ensure that the downloaded model is the expected one.

## Under the hood

- Added support for Parakeet’s offline NeMo transducer format without changing the existing online sherpa-onnx model paths.
- Improved model-source validation so the supported sherpa-onnx Parakeet conversion is accepted while raw, unsupported NVIDIA NeMo checkpoints remain excluded.
- Removed unused error and permission types and renamed several ambiguous internal types. This eliminates cross-target name collisions and makes error handling and model-runtime code easier to maintain without changing the app’s intended behaviour.

## Overview

Just Speak to It 2.44.0 adds a new Speech dashboard for understanding how you speak, using on-device analysis of your existing transcript history. It also improves the reliability of pairing and instant dictation under concurrent activity, while strengthening privacy and concurrency safeguards across the shared macOS and iOS code.

## Highlights

### New Speech dashboard

The macOS dashboard now includes a Speech section with cards for:

- Most-used words, phrases and longer expressions
- Filler and hedge words, including “um”, “uh”, “like”, “basically”, “sort of” and “you know”
- Speaking pace, including words per minute, averages, medians and distribution
- Vocabulary richness and words that are new or trending week over week
- Speech records, including total words, longest session and word of the month

Filler and hedge usage is shown as a rate per 1,000 words with a weekly trend, making it easier to spot changes over time.

The analysis uses the raw transcripts already saved in your history. It runs entirely on your device, makes no network requests, and stores its aggregate separately from sync payloads. Previously calculated results are retained, so the dashboard does not need to process your entire history every time it opens. Deleted or retention-expired transcripts are also removed from the calculations.

## Fixes

- Pairing changes are now serialised as complete transactions. Concurrent additions or removals should no longer overwrite one another, and concurrent pairing-code generation cannot create competing codes.
- Instant dictation now checks its enabled state safely when starting a session. Disabling dictation cannot race with session creation, and the consent flow enables dictation and creates its session atomically.
- Live transcription clients now protect mutable state correctly when work completes asynchronously, improving reliability during concurrent audio and network operations.

## Privacy and reliability

- Deepgram text-to-speech request handling is now shared between macOS and iOS while preserving existing platform-specific playback and error handling. API keys continue to be sent only in the authorisation header.
- SpeakCore now uses stricter concurrency checking, with the issues it identified resolved across storage, live transcription, audio conversion and local model code. This reduces the risk of unsafe cross-thread access and supports more maintainable future updates.
- Shared brand colours and Deepgram transport logic now have a single implementation, reducing the chance of macOS and iOS behaviour drifting apart.

## Overview

Just Speak to It now shows how quickly your dictation moves from speaking to text appearing in the target app. This release adds session-level latency tracking, dashboard insights, and a clearer delivery confirmation while keeping existing history items compatible.

## Highlights

- **See dictation latency in the Insights dashboard**
  - A new Latency card shows cold-start p50 and p95 times.
  - Per-provider metrics show p50 and p95 timings for the first words and for completing insertion after you stop speaking.
  - p50 represents the typical midpoint, while p95 helps reveal slower sessions.

- **Get immediate delivery feedback**
  - The HUD success message now reports the time taken to insert the final text, such as “Delivered in 320 ms”.

- **Track the full dictation pipeline**
  - Each new session records intervals from trigger to audio capture, first live partial text, first character inserted, and stop pressed to final insertion.
  - These timings are stored with history entries in whole milliseconds, preserving sub-second detail.

## Under the hood

- Existing history remains readable: older entries without latency data continue to decode normally.
- Latency calculations and percentile aggregation are covered by automated tests, improving reliability of the reported figures.

## Overview

Just Speak to It 2.42.0 adds per-app dictation profiles on macOS. You can now tailor transcription, polishing, language, and lexicon behaviour to the app you are using, with those settings applied only for the current dictation session. The release also strengthens safeguards around secure storage, device pairing, transport messages, and history synchronisation.

## Highlights

### Per-app dictation profiles

Create profiles in **Settings > Profiles** and associate them with specific apps using:

- A running-app picker
- Manually entered bundle IDs

A profile can override:

- Transcription model
- Spoken language
- LLM polishing, including whether it is enabled
- Polishing model
- Custom polishing instructions
- Output language
- Lexicon formatting options

When dictation starts, Just Speak to It checks the frontmost app and applies the first matching profile. Profile settings are session-only: your regular defaults are not changed, and they are restored when dictation ends.

While a profile is active, the recording HUD displays **“Profile: [name]”**, making it clear which configuration is being used. The Profiles tab is also available through the keyboard shortcut **⌘0**.

Profiles currently match applications by bundle ID. URL-pattern matching and profile synchronisation are not included in this release.

## Under the hood

Text-quality features—including the personal lexicon, learned autocorrection, word comparison, voice-command expansion, and pronunciation dictionary—now live in the shared core used by the app. This provides a more maintainable foundation for sharing the same behaviour across platforms while retaining the macOS-specific integration required for accessibility and pasteboard operations.

The release also adds broader protection for important synchronisation and device-connection paths, including:

- More complete secure-storage round-trip handling
- Rejection of malformed or incomplete transport messages
- Safer pairing-code and pairing-state handling
- Guards against unavailable cloud services and stalled history acknowledgements
- More predictable history reconciliation when changes, deletions, duplicates, or clock differences are involved

These checks improve resilience without changing the normal dictation workflow.

## What's Changed
* refactor: unify OpenRouter HTTP client in SpeakCore by @bravostation in https://github.com/crmitchelmore/justspeaktoit/pull/625
* fix(transport): validate HelloMessage.protocolVersion on hello by @bravostation in https://github.com/crmitchelmore/justspeaktoit/pull/629

## Overview

The iOS launch screen has been refreshed with an adaptive Just Speak to It brand mark, providing a more consistent appearance when the app starts in light or dark mode.

## Highlights

- Updated the iOS launch screen with the refreshed Just Speak to It branding.
- Added light and dark variants of the brand mark so the launch screen adapts to the device’s appearance setting.

## Overview

Just Speak to It 2.40.0 improves accessibility across the app and makes transcription and history handling more resilient. VoiceOver users get clearer control descriptions and state announcements, while the interface now better respects system motion, transparency, and text-size preferences.

## Highlights

- **Improved VoiceOver support**
  - Recording controls in the main view and dashboard now provide clearer labels, hints, and button traits.
  - The sidebar exposes the selected item and its value correctly.
  - History import and clear controls now have explicit labels and hints.
  - Personal corrections candidate buttons are identified as buttons with descriptive labels.
  - Voice output now announces its synthesising state and identifies the stop control correctly.
  - HUD phase changes generate accessibility announcements, making transcription progress easier to follow without looking at the screen.

- **Better support for accessibility preferences**
  - The HUD respects Reduce Motion and Reduce Transparency settings.
  - Text sizes are constrained where necessary to preserve usable layouts at larger Dynamic Type sizes.
  - Frequently changing HUD content is marked appropriately for assistive technologies.

## Reliability and performance

- History file operations now run through a dedicated storage actor rather than on the main application actor. This keeps disk reads and writes separate from UI state updates and makes snapshot, append, rewrite, and clear operations properly coordinated.
- Live streaming shutdown now uses an explicit stopping state and a bounded flush that waits for no more than one second. This prevents a flush from waiting indefinitely when a session is ending.
- Secure storage no longer emits routine output every time it is initialised. Detailed keychain diagnostics are available only when `SPEAK_DEBUG_KEYCHAIN=1` is enabled.

## Under the hood

- The shared model catalogue types and streaming lifecycle code have been separated into focused components, making future provider and catalogue changes easier to maintain.
- Application dependencies can now be replaced with a test environment, allowing isolated UI testing without constructing the full application graph.
- The project now includes checksum verification and additional coverage for streaming and accessibility behaviour.

## Overview

This release makes transcription language selection more consistent across Just Speak to It on macOS and iOS. Your chosen language is now shared by the app’s transcription settings and is passed through to supported live transcription services, while privacy and telemetry information has been clarified.

## Highlights

- **Shared transcription language preference**
  - Choose your preferred transcription language from the transcription settings.
  - The preference is used consistently across the app’s transcription workflows on macOS and iOS.
  - Soniox live transcription now receives the selected language, helping it transcribe speech using the language you chose.
  - Settings have been reorganised so the language preference is presented in the appropriate general settings area.

## Privacy and security

- Updated the privacy and security documentation to align telemetry disclosures across the app’s published materials.
- Refined the app’s privacy declarations and related documentation to make its data and telemetry practices clearer.

## Overview

This maintenance release improves the reliability of live transcription and audio recording on macOS. Start and stop transitions are better ordered, failed transcription launches clean up safely, and recording persistence is more robust when reads and writes overlap.

## Highlights

- **More reliable live transcription sessions**  
  Recognition callbacks are now coordinated with transcription start and stop operations. This helps prevent events from an earlier session from interfering with a newer one during rapid transitions or backend changes.

- **Safer recovery when transcription cannot start**  
  If the Sherpa ONNX transcription process fails to launch or audio setup fails, Just Speak to It now follows the same cleanup path. This leaves the app in a consistent state and avoids attempting to terminate a process that never started.

- **Improved transcription diagnostics**  
  Sherpa ONNX error output is kept separately for each transcription session, with bounded memory usage. Output is also captured when the process exits, so relevant diagnostics are less likely to be lost or mixed with messages from a previous session.

- **More dependable recording persistence**  
  Recording storage now handles close and write operations more safely when they occur at the same time, reducing the risk of inconsistent persistence during recording finalisation.

## Under the hood

- Replaced timing-dependent recording persistence race tests with tests that verify the actual concurrent interleaving.
- Simplified and strengthened live-transcriber state management to preserve correct ordering across session changes.
- Improved handling of partial text encoding in process output, preventing valid output split across reads from being discarded.

## Overview

This release makes device-to-device configuration transfers safer and fixes an iOS issue that could leave imported credentials unavailable to the app. It also moves Deepgram Flux onto the shared streaming transcription architecture, making live transcription behaviour more consistent across providers.

## Highlights

### Safer QR configuration transfers

Configuration exports now protect API keys and other credentials with authenticated AES-GCM encryption.

- The exporting device displays an 8-character, one-time code alongside the QR code.
- The code is required to decrypt the transfer but is not included in the QR data.
- Transfers are rejected if the code is incorrect, the payload has been tampered with, its version is unsupported, or it is more than 10 minutes old.
- Credentials are not written until the transfer has passed all validation checks.
- Existing legacy XOR-based transfers can still be imported, but new exports always use the encrypted format.

This means that a photograph or scan of a QR code alone is no longer sufficient to recover the credentials it contains.

### Deepgram Flux uses the shared live transcription client

Deepgram Flux has been integrated with SpeakCore’s shared streaming client and transcription handling. This standardises how streaming providers finish sessions and accumulate transcripts, improving consistency in live transcription and making the underlying provider integrations easier to maintain.

## Fixes

### QR imports now use the correct iOS credential store

The iOS QR transfer flow previously used a different keychain service from the app’s canonical credential store. As a result, successfully imported keys could be invisible to the app afterwards.

Both QR export and import paths now use the canonical storage location, so credentials transferred to iOS are available where the app expects them.

## Under the hood

- Key derivation for encrypted QR transfers is based on PBKDF2-SHA256 with a random salt and a one-time code.
- The transfer envelope authenticates its metadata as well as its contents, so changes to its version or timestamp cause decryption to fail.
- Shared streaming-client contracts and transcript accumulation are now covered by common tests, helping prevent provider-specific differences from returning in future updates.

## Overview

Just Speak to It 2.37.0 improves transcription reliability, history performance, and App Store behaviour, while adding a faster way to reuse your latest transcription. It also makes provider configuration more consistent across macOS and iOS.

## Highlights

- **Paste your latest transcription with a shortcut.** Press **⌥⌘V** to insert the most recent history item into the frontmost app. The shortcut uses the post-processed text when available and follows your configured output method, including the existing accessibility and clipboard fallback behaviour. It can be rebound in **Shortcuts** settings.
- **More reliable live transcription.** Audio processing now moves away from the real-time microphone callback, reducing the risk of dropped audio while recording, resampling, encoding, saving, or sending audio to a provider. Recording writes are also coordinated safely when a session stops or is cancelled.
- **Safer session stopping and restarting.** Improvements to stop handling prevent an old session’s timeout from interfering with a new one, ensure queued audio is finished before finalisation, and reduce races in streaming provider connections.
- **Faster history handling.** macOS history changes now use an append-only log instead of rewriting the entire history file for every operation. Filtering is cached in the history view, and iOS history synchronisation batches incoming updates to reduce repeated file writes. History remains recoverable from the previous file format, including after an incomplete final log entry.
- **Deepgram batch models are now available in the model picker.** The `nova`, `enhanced`, and `base` batch models can now be selected wherever they are supported.

## Fixes

- **App Store builds no longer attempt direct-download installation tasks**, avoiding inappropriate DMG cleanup and `/Applications` operations in the sandboxed app.
- **Send to Mac failures are now shown instead of being ignored.** If the listener cannot start, the setting is switched back off, the reason is logged, and the Settings card displays the reported error. Failed listeners also clear their active connections.
- **API key errors are more accurate.** A genuinely missing key is distinguished from locked-keychain or other access failures, so existing keys are no longer incorrectly reported as missing. Missing-key prompts now cover all supported live providers.
- **Configuration transfer is shared between macOS and iOS.** QR transfers use the same key and settings collection, with iOS now including OpenAI text-to-speech and Azure Speech API keys.
- Sensitive credentials are fully redacted from API validation diagnostics, and a key-derived value is no longer written to logs.

## Under the hood

Provider catalog and validation logic now have a single source of truth, reducing the chance that a model appears in one place but cannot be routed correctly. Shared live-transcription handling also makes future reliability fixes consistent across providers.

## Overview

This release improves recording reliability on iOS, particularly for sessions started from the Action Button, Siri, or Shortcuts. Transcriptions are less likely to lose trailing words, silently use the wrong provider, or leave the microphone active after an error.

## Highlights

- **More reliable provider selection on cold launch:** Recording now waits for your API keys to load before starting. This prevents headless launches from mistakenly falling back to Apple Speech because the keys were not ready.
- **Clearer fallback information:** If on-device transcription is still used, the app now reports the fallback, logs it, and shows “(no API key)” in the Live Activity’s provider line.
- **Recording errors are now surfaced:** Mid-session failures appear as an alert instead of being shown only in the Live Activity. The recording is stopped cleanly, the microphone is released, and the transcript collected so far is preserved.
- **Fewer lost words when stopping:** Deepgram and ElevenLabs sessions now allow up to one second for the final transcription result after stopping. This gives trailing speech time to arrive before the connection closes.
- **More complete live transcripts:** Partial results now consistently contain the full display transcript across transcription providers. Live Activity text and word counts no longer reset with each utterance, and the final transcript is less likely to contain only the last segment.
- **Safer repeated controls:** Pressing stop twice no longer duplicates history or replaces the clipboard with stale text. Concurrent start requests are also guarded to prevent duplicate sessions.

## Under the hood

- Shared recording state and word counts are now written at a controlled rate during recording, with a guaranteed final update when the session stops. This reduces unnecessary updates while keeping the final Live Activity and transcript state accurate.
- Streaming clients now use a common finalisation process, including Deepgram’s close-stream message and early completion when the final result is received.
- Session state and partial text are cleared after a completed stop, reducing the chance of stale data carrying into a later recording.
